title: One importable unit
explanation: A module groups related Python code. Often it is a .py file; built-in and extension modules also exist.

title: Organize related modules
explanation: A package is a module that can contain submodules. A regular package usually has __init__.py; namespace packages can omit it.
analogy: Think: a folder of related recipes.

title: Reusable tools for your program
explanation: A library is reusable code, often made of modules and packages. lib is a common abbreviation, not a special Python keyword.
example: import math     # from Python’s standard library
analogy: Think: a toolbox you choose tools from.

title: A structure for building an app
explanation: A framework supplies an application structure and runs parts of the workflow. Your code fits into that structure, for example Django views.
example: Framework calls your handler when a request arrives
analogy: Think: a workshop with an established workflow.

title: Different labels, related roles
explanation: Modules and packages describe code organization. Libraries and frameworks describe how reusable code is used. These labels can overlap.
example: Install third-party tools with pip; import names in Python.
analogy: Python includes its standard library. Django is installed separately.
